chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleym, the mawla of Tarbal, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who slept with a slave girl of his, and that he used to send her regarding his needs, and that she became pregnant, and that news of immorality about her reached him. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When she gives birth, he keeps the child, so he should not sell him, and he makes for him a share in his house.'

He said, 'It was said to him: A man slept with a slave girl of his, and that he did not used to send her regarding his needs, and that he accused her, and she became pregnant.' So he said: 'When she gives birth, he keeps the child and does not sell him, and he makes for him a share from his house and his wealth, and this is not the like of that.'

key_terms.يَطَأُ: He sleeps with / has intercourse with

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the child of a slave girl impregnated by her master in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'Umm al-Walad' (mother of the child) in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring that a slave girl's child inherits from the father regardless of whether the relationship was casual or formalized through task delegation. It highlights the juristic distinction between the two scenarios to determine the extent of the child's inheritance share, emphasizing the child's freedom and right to a portion of the master's estate upon his death.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleym Mowla Tarbal, from Hareyz,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who slept with a slave girl of his and he used to send her regarding his needs, and she became pregnant, and (news of) immorality about her reached him. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When she gives birth, keep the child, but he should not sell him, and should make for him a share in his house’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘It was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man slept with a slave girl of his and he did not used to send her regarding his needs, and he accused her, and she became pregnant’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When she gives birth, he keeps the child and does not sell him, and he makes for him a share from his house, and his wealth, and this is not the like of that’.
